key_insight: In humans, eye saccades are accompanied by widespread saccade-related evoked potentials (SREPs) that appear to support visual memory encoding, especially in frontoparietal cortex.
clinical_relevance: These findings may help explain how active vision interacts with memory formation and could inform future neural markers of encoding during eye-movement-based tasks.
method: Combined eye tracking with intracranial local field potential recordings in humans during memory tasks
Analyzed saccade-locked cortical evoked activity across brain regions
Used machine learning to test whether pre-saccadic oscillations and SREPs predicted memory outcomes
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that SREPs emerged earliest and strongest in lateral temporal cortex, and that pre-saccadic oscillations plus SREPs predicted recognition memory but not saccade direction.
watch_item: Because the study is based on intracranial recordings in a limited human sample, broader generalizability and practical use as a biomarker will need further validation.
paper_title: Mind's eye: widespread saccade-related evoked potentials support visual memory encoding in humans
